package.description: Claude Code and Codex quota in the Windows system tray.

en-US.description: Claude Code and Codex quota in the Windows system tray.
en-US.longDescription:
A bead in your tray fills up as you burn through your 5-hour and weekly windows for
Claude Code and Codex. Click it for every window, its percentage and when it resets;
it turns amber at 60 %, red at 85 %, and warns you once per window per reset before
you hit the wall.

By default it reads nothing but local files: no credentials, no network. Codex numbers
come from the session log Codex already writes. Claude numbers come from a small
status-line wrapper that records what your status line already receives and then runs
the status line you had; installing it is a button in the settings page, never a side
effect of installing this. An opt-in "detailed windows" mode adds the model-scoped
weekly windows from the official usage endpoint, reading the sign-in token in memory
for one request and writing it nowhere.

The tray writes one file, ~/.nazar/limits.json, which holds four numbers per window
and no token, account identifier or e-mail. Six interface languages: English, Türkçe,
中文, 한국어, Русский, Español.
en-US.name: nazar-tray
